issues.reason: Thematic roles states the mechanical rule that an oblique's head is the preposition actually used — 'in stays In; During renders only the word during' — so During for surface 'in' is exactly the barred near-fit synonym head.

Cardinality's 'Both dogs barked' pattern is explicit that a counted plural with a distributive predicate keeps the group + count + group event AND adds the per-member rule over (PartOf $x <group>); competing in a round is distributive, and the rule is absent.

The reviewer's own q2 concedes there is no licensed carrier for totality 'all' on a predicate nominal, and the instruction set's standing direction in gap territory is to 'leave the unrepresentable adverbial out rather than mis-slot it' — the dropped word leaves nothing false or over-asserted behind.

gaps_confirmed: exhaustive/totality 'all' on a predicate nominal ('the round is all oral examination') — QuantifierPhrase ranges over a subject's members and Degree needs an adjectival scale, so neither fits
bare pronominal 'both' with no antecedent — 'both' is defined as a definite count reusing already-introduced members, and the no-antecedent pronoun rule covers he/she/it/they only
ordinal over a sequence of like nouns ('the third round') — the Ordinal scale is defined as the associated event or an explicit -est dimension, neither of which exists here
new_gaps: participation-'in' whose object is itself an eventuality ('compete in the third round'): the preposition-named oblique records the PP, but nothing temporally nests the two eventualities, since During is reserved for the surface word 'during'
repair_summary: Replaced (During sk_compete_1 sk_round_1) with the surface-preposition oblique (In sk_compete_1 sk_round_1); added the per-member distribution rule over (PartOf $x sk_group_1) carrying the same class, Agent, Future and In atoms, at (STV 1.0 0.9) per the counted-plural pattern.
notes: The group event and count are kept alongside the rule, as the 'Both dogs barked' exemplar does. Nothing else in the parse was touched.
